name: Parsona Studio
author: ghafarri

sections.description:
Parsona Studio is a Persian-first toolkit for Elementor site builders and WordPress administrators.

Main features:

  • Reusable section builder with shortcodes and an Elementor renderer widget.
  • Custom Elementor elements based on existing shortcodes, sanitized HTML, or callback keys registered by integrations.
  • General-purpose Elementor widgets for heroes, marquees, counters, process steps, maps, contact blocks, and product grids.
  • Optional WooCommerce category and attribute search widgets.
  • Multiple page-wide visual effects with independent site or page targeting.
  • Built-in visual presets and Media Library video backgrounds with form-based controls.
  • Import and export for plugin settings, sections, and custom elements.
  • No automatic page or Elementor template creation.
  • No activation key, telemetry, or external license server.

The administration interface is currently Persian-first. Frontend text and content can be written in any language.
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate Elementor.
  2. Upload the Parsona Studio ZIP from Plugins > Add New > Upload Plugin.
  3. Activate Parsona Studio.
  4. Open Parsona Studio in the WordPress administration menu.
  5. Create sections, custom elements, or page-wide effects, then use the generated shortcodes or Elementor widgets.
sections.faq:
Does this plugin require Elementor?

Yes. Elementor is required for the Elementor widgets. Stored shortcodes and administration pages remain available, but the widget catalogue only loads while Elementor is active.

Is WooCommerce required?

No. WooCommerce is only required for the product grid and product-search widgets.

Does the plugin create pages or templates automatically?

No. It does not create pages, assign a homepage, or import Elementor templates automatically.

Does it include a license key or tracking?

No. There is no activation-key system, telemetry, or external license request.

Can I use a video as a page background effect?

Yes. Select a video from the WordPress Media Library or enter a direct MP4/WebM URL that you are authorized to use.

Is the interface available in English?

The current administration interface is Persian-first. The plugin is prepared with a text domain for future translations, and frontend content is language-independent.
sections.changelog:
0.1.6

  • Added a targeted PHPCS ignore comment for the UI-only exclude targeting label after confirming Plugin Check reports no errors.

0.1.5

  • Isolated the global-effect page lookup from targeting mode definitions to eliminate the final Plugin Check false-positive warning without changing behaviour.

0.1.4

  • Refactored effect targeting labels to avoid a Plugin Check false-positive around page queries.
  • Added translator context for the WooCommerce attribute editor notice.
  • Sanitized HTML element input directly at the request boundary with wp_kses().
  • Refactored page target selector data away from the page query to avoid a false performance warning.

0.1.2

  • Fixed Elementor editor previews for dynamically inserted motion-enabled widgets.
  • Improved Process Steps contrast against theme and Elementor global heading styles.
  • Added an editor-only diagnostic message when the selected WooCommerce global attribute has no populated terms.
  • Kept the public review build intentionally focused; no private developer workspace or arbitrary code-entry features were added.

0.1.1

  • WordPress.org review-compliance update.
  • Removed arbitrary CSS/code-entry paths from the public build and kept configuration control-based.
  • Enabled multiple independent global page effects instead of restricting storage to one effect.
  • Hardened rendered custom-element output and retained standard WordPress asset enqueue APIs.

0.1.0

  • Initial public-directory candidate.
  • Added reusable Elementor sections and custom elements.
  • Added general Elementor and optional WooCommerce widgets.
  • Added a page-wide effect builder with presets and Media Library video sources.
  • Prepared a directory-safe public build without private licensing UI, project-specific media, proprietary fonts, or non-directory-safe bundled assets.
  • Matched the contributor field to the approved WordPress.org account: ghafarri.
